components.name: Ambulance transport from residence to hospital

reason: Chest pain is a listed sign of cardiac distress meeting the emergency presumption, and all three agents support coverage; residence-to-hospital is a covered origin and destination.

Multiple therapy disciplines (PT and OT) were provided, daily physician contact and measurable functional gains are shown, and therapy minutes are consistent with roughly 3 hours daily; the undocumented items are not enough to defeat coverage.
No agent supports skilled need: oral medications and caregiver-given insulin are not skilled, and no ongoing instability is shown for either period.

components.name: Home health skilled nursing visits (eight visits over three and one-half weeks)

reason: Coumadin dosage was adjusted twice with INR above the safe range, so prothrombin monitoring and skilled observation were reasonable and necessary, and the plan of care specified type and frequency.

All agents find necessity unsettled; transport was for nausea with treat-and-release, and the caregiver's inability to use her SUV does not show other transport was contraindicated. Mileage follows the transport.

components.name: Fixed wing air ambulance transport (A0430) and air miles to the nearest facility
Extra 107 air miles beyond nearest appropriate facility (A0435)

reason: All agents find air transport not supported: the appellant concedes ground transport was reasonable, vital signs were stable, and a closer capable facility existed, so neither the air base rate nor the excess mileage is covered.

components.name: Ground ambulance transfer from Proctor Hospital to St. Francis

reason: A hospital-to-hospital transfer is payable, and the on-call neurosurgeon recommended transfer to neuro ICU for a hemorrhagic stroke, showing the originating hospital lacked the needed service; the nearest-facility question is unresolved but nothing contradicts it.

The cardiologist states ambulance with cardiac monitoring was necessary three days after pacemaker and lead replacement for a dependent patient, which supports that other transport was contraindicated despite his ability to walk.
Both OT and PT were planned daily, the patient had complex medical needs, and measurable functional improvement was documented; unstated intensity and paperwork gaps do not outweigh this.

components.name: Inpatient hospital admission and resulting stay

reason: The inpatient decision was recorded as an error and reverted to observation, the discharge summary says overnight observation, and observation orders do not meet inpatient admission requirements.

The run sheet records the destination as a clinic, and transport to a physician-directed clinic is not covered; the appellant's claim that it was a hospital or SNF is unsupported. Mileage follows the transport.

Documented functional limitations and taxing effort to leave home support homebound status, and infrequent absences for adult day care and doctor visits do not defeat it; all three agents support coverage.

The beneficiary was formally admitted to inpatient status after transfer for a higher level of care with chest pain, new T-wave inversion and extensive cardiac history, and the stay approached two midnights; missing order details are not shown to be absent.

components.name: Air ambulance transfer to Via Christi, Wichita

reason: The transferring hospital lacked a cardiologist, two other hospitals also lacked one, and the patient became progressively unstable; cardiac care is a listed specialized service, so the transfer is supported despite the unresolved nearest-facility dispute.
Coverage does not depend solely on improvement potential; a physician-signed plan ordered dysphagia therapy with documented assessment and steady measurable gains, and all agents support coverage.
No agent finds skilled need established: the facts show only certifications with no reasonable potential for change, instability, or visit-level documentation after about sixteen months of care.

components.name: Home health nursing and aide services

reason: All agents find the issues unsettled: the beneficiary leaves home four days weekly independently with no licensed or certified day care shown, and the record does not show she cannot do personal care or needs a plan of care for aide tasks.

components.name: Skilled nursing visits (mediplanner and aide oversight)

reason: All agents do not support coverage: filling a mediplanner and overseeing aides is not skilled, no potential for change is documented, and aide hours exceed the 28-hour limit.

Agents' passages address only non-covered-related services and none is identified, so nothing defeats coverage; the case facts show admission after complicated hernia repair with significant pulmonary disease, oxygen, pulmonary assessments and spirometry.
Nurses assessed, treated and taught wound care for pressure ulcer and wounds in a diabetic patient, which is skilled wound care, and visit notes document each episode through healing.
All agents do not support coverage: family administered medications and monitored glucose, aides were involved, and the record has only the appellant's assertions and two glucose readings.
Gait training and range of motion are skilled PT, the plan of care ordered type and frequency, and objective measures documented improvement from 7/28 to 18/28; all agents support coverage.
